To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Simplifying antiretoviral therapy (ART) for clinically stable people livng with HIV (PLWHIV) is important, but insufficient to meet all of their health care needs; 2) DSD 1.1, a patient-centric approach, is a promising avenue for achieving such coverage; 3) The lack of coordination of care between HIV programs and other chronic care services puts a burden not only on the health system but also on PLHIV; and

the lack of coordination between vertical programs for people living with HIV, tuberculosis, and family planning, and noncommunicable disease services puts a burden both on the patients, and on the health systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) How can we improve the health outcomes of PLHIV through a patient-centered, integrated, and inclusive DSD model?
the following question: What is the best way to organize and deliver care to people living with HIV?
the question of what it means to have a good life and to live a good life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DSD 2 is a more inclusive, truly patient-centered approach to chronic disease care that is more likely to achieve the health outcomes and efficiencies desired by all stakeholders.

DSD 2.o is an opportunity for the vertical HIV program, the vertical TB program and the vertical family planning programs and the relatively weaker noncommunicative disease programs to achieve greater collective impact by integrating strong vertical programs and relatively weaker non communicative disease programs.
DSD 2.o is the way to go for PLHIV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the current approach to differentiated service delivery is insufficient to meet the needs of patients and that a more comprehensive approach that is patient-centered and truly inclusive of the needs of people living with HIV is needed to achieve the goals of the HIV and Universal Coverage agendas.
the DSD 2 framework can help countries to achieve the SDG3 targets for HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis and other NCDs, and to achieve the SDGs more broadly.
we are advocating for an inclusive and truly patient-centered care for PLHIF.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DSD 2.o can be achieved by integrating services that are already being delivered to PLHIV into a single platform, rather than by creating entirely new service delivery systems.
DSD 2,0 is not only feasible but is also a logical next step in the evolution of differentiated care.

the current DSD model for HIV care is insufficient to meet the full range of health care needs of PLHIV, and that the health system needs to be reorganized to better serve them and the broader population.
